alternative_architecture.description: Reorganize around a thin, single-feature delivery ledger. State: stable requirement IDs/revisions plus Git, small near-frontier contracts, append-only attempt journals, and delivery receipts. Planning: human selects one feature; a planner and Unity scanner validate one contract and its actual paths/GUIDs. Execution: one writable provider in an isolated worktree. Validation: deterministic diff/scope checks, Unity compile, EditMode/PlayMode tests, exact committed-scene inspection, semantic review, and human playtesting. Recovery: preserve branch commits and stage journals, resume from the failed stage, and circuit-break after bounded repairs. Unity integration: serialize only through approved editor/builder operations, retain `.meta` identity, run one host Unity job at a time, and compare canonical asset bytes before/after tests.
alternative_architecture.why_better: This preserves the good safety boundaries but removes global reconciliation, provider parity, artifact generation, GitHub synchronization, and parallel scheduling from the critical path. Requirement-level revisions prevent unrelated GDD edits from invalidating every delivered task, while a task preflight prevents stale Unity paths and GUIDs from entering execution. Most importantly, it produces gameplay evidence before investing further in platform machinery.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The core topology is good: bounded workers, Git as integrated truth, deterministic validation, runtime feedback, immutable evidence, and human design/merge authority. The current composition is partially unsound because it lacks an end-to-end writable Unity delivery lane and duplicates mutable project facts across too many stores. An ordinary human-approved scene relocation already left canon, 16 contracts, project requirements, and resource locks pointing at a deleted asset while structural validation still passed.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: No real gameplay task has passed through the current AgentRuntime/TaskExecution architecture. Actual implementation quality, Unity failure rate, repair cost, and end-to-end cycle time remain unmeasured; the camera evidence predates the production execution lane.
do_not_build_yet: Parallel workers, generalized worktree scheduling, or merge queues.
Provider fallback or additional provider-comparison/review machinery.
A general Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority platform before a real task is blocked by missing design.
Style evaluation or automated artifact generation.
A broad incremental project scanner; add only the Unity/task preflight needed by the next slice.

evidence.observation: The checked-out clean tree is exactly the required frozen commit 9f2485dca1b61360e6d02810adc71e021346496e.

Read-only execution of `taskcontrol validate` passed structurally with 37 active contracts, but autonomous dispatch remained disabled. NSC-023 derived `conformant`; NSC-003 derived `not_delivered`. No Unity tests were executed during this review.
Production ExecutionCrew orchestration, Unity execution, task selection, readiness, dispatch, Git workflow, merging, and provider fallback are explicitly unimplemented.
Both live provider adapters reject repository writing and approved command execution, so AgentRuntime cannot implement a gameplay task.
TaskExecution only binds a task identity to one invocation; it explicitly owns no selection, Git, Unity, GER, evidence publication, or completion transition.
Commit 484e66a moved the populated authoritative scene and its `.meta` identity to `Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity`; commit 86af98f added path/GUID safeguards.
Sixteen active task contracts still cite the deleted `Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity` path.
The GDD still declares the deleted nested scene canonical and the populated `Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity` non-canonical, despite the later human-approved relocation.
Project requirements and the shared scene resource group retain the same obsolete path, so future lock acquisition would not protect the real scene.
The graph validator checks resource-key consistency but not whether `repo-file`, `unity-scene`, repository-evidence, or GUID targets exist.
The scene-location smoke test correctly protects uniqueness and GUID 92dbd0a3e6c18e245896a66c5120379d, but only scans active C# for obsolete references; it does not cover canon or task metadata.

NSC-023 is reported conformant even though its bound contract still contains stale scene repository evidence; its evidence record separately points at the current scene. The evaluator verifies hashes, gates, and listed surfaces, not factual consistency of repository-evidence prose.

Conformance binds the normalized hash of the entire GDD. Any GDD edit stales existing evidence, while only a contract hash/revision change produces `needs_replan`. Conformance surfaces are manually enumerated.
A passing camera EditMode suite previously invoked the saving production builder and rewrote the canonical tracked scene. The non-saving builder seam and clean runner were created in response.
The camera twice passed static evaluation but failed human Unity testing for direction, following, and framing; a later refiner also claimed implementation while making no asset change.

Since August 21, reachable history contains roughly 205 commits, only three of which touch Assets; those Asset changes concern test safety and scene centralization rather than a new gameplay feature. The repository has 303 pipeline/task/AI-document files versus 51 tracked Asset files.

NSC-003 is classified as `single_agent` despite spanning Input Actions, pointer projection, locomotion, restriction/reset/suspend interfaces, builder wiring, serialized-scene integration, and unresolved input arbitration. Current PlayerMovement still directly polls `Keyboard.current`.
Unity 6000.1.8f1 is pinned and the Input System is installed, but Build Settings contain no scenes and the required Tilemap/AI Navigation packages are not configured yet.

gdd_iteration_concerns: The architecture currently treats the whole GDD as one versioned unit. An unrelated wording, balance, or room edit will require revalidation of every task whose evidence binds the previous document hash.

A semantic GDD change can require a new contract, different dependencies, implementation rollback, or cancellation. Returning only `needs_revalidation` against the old contract frames design evolution incorrectly.
There are no stable requirement IDs/revisions in canon and no implemented causal mapping from changed requirements to contracts, code/assets, tests, and downstream obligations.

Reconciliation is correctly immutable, but the reviewed graph-delta/apply process for later changes is not implemented. The scene relocation demonstrates that ordinary repository evolution can bypass synchronization.
Repository/process facts should not be copied into root design canon unless maintained transactionally. Canon currently contradicts Git about the authoritative scene.

The future change flow should classify edits as editorial, tuning, additive, changed, or removed; update only affected contracts; supersede contracts when meaning changes; and preserve unaffected delivery evidence.
human_intervention_points: Choose actual product priority; graph order and apparent readiness are not sufficient.
Resolve NSC-003 input arbitration, click-versus-hold semantics, destination replacement/cancellation, arrival/pathing behavior, and restriction ownership before execution.
Approve normative GDD changes and reviewed contract additions, revisions, supersessions, or cancellations.
Inspect scene/prefab references, Inspector assignments, asset imports, and serialized diffs in the Unity Editor.
Run PlayMode checks for game feel, framing, pointer behavior, animation/readability, balance, and Console errors.
Perform Windows build inspection and approve package/build-setting changes.
Review and merge the task branch; automatic merge is not currently justified.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Deep adversarial freezing of provider JSON subtypes and polymorphic containers protects a future hostile/malformed adapter boundary more than an experienced Unity delivery failure.
Cross-provider ArchitectureReview provenance, latest-pointer, and resume support improves review infrastructure but not gameplay throughput.
Provider fallback and cross-provider-equivalent budgeting are future operational concerns.
Parallel worktree claims, GitHub dashboards, merge queues, and continuous scheduling protect a later multi-worker system.
Artifact Authority, generated-design GER, and style evaluation protect future content-generation cases; the current graph contains no initial artifact task and no demonstrated blocking artifact flow.
missing_components: A small approved NSC-003 child contract with resolved input behavior.
A writable, bounded Implementer path using one provider and an isolated branch/worktree.
Task-scoped orchestration from contract to implementation result, deterministic diff, validation, repair, and escalation.
A host Unity execution bridge around the existing clean PowerShell runner.
Deterministic task preflight that validates referenced files, canonical scenes, `.meta` GUIDs, Input Action identities, packages, builder ownership, and Build Settings.
Automatic capture of actual changed paths and scope violations from Git rather than provider claims.
A reviewed evidence publisher that binds actual clean Unity XML, commit/tree, changed surfaces, human approval, and integrated commit.
Requirement-level GDD change-impact analysis and deterministic reviewed contract-delta application.
A derived readiness policy based on current conformance and dependency state; it should remain human-dispatched initially.

deliverables: Record a human-approved movement micro-brief resolving click/hold input arbitration, destination replacement/cancellation, arrival/pathing, and UI/spell/door click ownership.
Correct the authoritative scene path in canon, affected task/resource metadata, and validation so this drift cannot recur silently.

Supersede or split NSC-003 into a bounded first contract: Input Actions-based pointer projection plus click/hold player movement. Leave restriction/reset/suspend integration as a follow-up if it cannot remain independently testable.
Add only the minimal one-task writable runner needed to invoke one provider in an isolated worktree and capture the real Git diff.
Implement the movement slice in PlayerMovement, Input Actions, the builder, and the authoritative committed scene without regenerating `.meta` identity.
Add isolated component/PlayMode tests plus direct committed-scene conformance checks, run them through the clean Unity host runner, and complete a human feel/input check.
Merge through human review and publish one exact delivery record; use it to prove the first evidence-derived dependency/readiness transition.
next_slice.proof_of_value: One approved gameplay contract travels from planned to implemented, cleanly Unity-tested, human-playtested, merged, evidence-published, and currently conformant at HEAD. Measure elapsed time, model invocations, repair count, human minutes, and escaped defects. That is the first credible evidence that the architecture makes development materially faster.
next_slice.title: NSC-003A — End-to-End Mouse Movement Delivery Lane
next_slice.why: This is the smallest slice that exercises the actual value chain and unlocks spells and door interaction. If infrastructure additions were forbidden, the first autonomous failure would be immediate: current providers cannot write or execute commands. With an ordinary human-driven coding agent, the first semantic failure would be NSC-003's unresolved input contract; after implementation, Unity execution and evidence publication would still be manual. This slice exposes and closes all three gaps without building the later platform.

observed_failure_solutions: Runtime Unity feedback feeding GER solved camera direction, following, and framing defects missed by static semantic review.
The no-op progress guard prevented a refiner's unchanged `implemented` claim from being accepted and charged it against the repair budget.
The non-saving in-memory builder seam separated builder capability from canonical serialized state and stopped tests from saving the production scene.
Direct committed-scene tests, byte comparison, and the clean runner address the experienced destructive passing-test incident.
Moving the scene with its `.meta`, asserting one authoritative scene, and checking the GUID address the duplicate-scene/asset-identity incident.
Immutable reconciliation runs, recovery scripts, bounded retries, and deterministic finding identities address actual max-turn, timeout, interrupted-run, and ordering failures visible in history.

Schema-v2 contracts and committed conformance evidence prevent a mutable task status or worker claim from becoming completion truth, although autonomous dispatch had not yet experienced that failure in production.
Production GDDRAG fixes the demonstrated staleness of the older Assignment 4 index, while correctly not claiming top-k coverage completeness.
overengineering: The project implemented two live provider adapters and migrated an eight-role architecture-review consumer before enabling one provider to write a gameplay change.

The accepted staged plan requires both adapters and full ExecutionCrew roles before the first real provider-interchangeable task proof; that ordering optimizes abstraction confidence ahead of product throughput.

Global multi-model reconciliation, verification, streaming refinement, recovery, migrations, and immutable histories consumed substantial effort for a 37-contract bootstrap. They should not become the normal response to iterative GDD edits.
There are multiple overlapping architecture/status documents with already-stale milestone claims. Operational status should be generated from code where possible.
The repository's recent commit/file ratio shows infrastructure becoming a second product: extensive pipeline churn has not produced a post-camera gameplay feature.
Provider trust-boundary hardening is technically strong, but much of its depth has lower current expected value than a writable task lane, Unity preflight, and one real gameplay delivery.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries: approved GDD/feature decisions define intent; task contracts define bounded work and gates; Git defines integrated code/assets; attempt journals define transient execution; evidence receipts plus current Git derive conformance; humans own ambiguous design, visual/feel approval, and merge authority.
Necessary separation: generic AgentRuntime must not own NSC task identity, and TaskExecution audit artifacts must not become completion evidence. The ADR-039 direction is correct.

Duplicated responsibility: authoritative scene paths and other repository facts appear in GDD prose, task repository evidence, exclusive-resource keys, project requirements, RAG chunks, current-state documents, and conformance surfaces.

The living graph is called operational state, but schema v2 intentionally contains no operational status and readiness is disabled. It is currently a contract/dependency catalog, not an operational work graph.

Manual conformance-surface selection can under-approximate Unity dependencies. A package, Input Action, prefab, ProjectSetting, referenced ScriptableObject, or builder dependency omitted from the receipt can change without invalidating conformance.
Reconciliation history should remain audit history, but it should not be a prerequisite authority layer for routine local changes. A requirement/task delta plus human approval is enough.
GitHub should remain a projection/dashboard if introduced; it must not duplicate contract, evidence, or conformance authority.
strong_decisions: One bounded worker and human merge authority before parallelism are appropriate for Unity's shared serialized assets.
Workers and provider adapters produce claims, never test, merge, readiness, or completion truth.
Task contracts are separated from mutable completion status, and committed Git objects—not a dirty working copy—drive conformance evaluation.
Exact commit/tree, artifact blob, task revision, canon hash, and human approval binding make evidence auditable.
Unity tests must start and finish with a clean tree, parse XML, preserve logs, and report exact Unity version and limitations.
Builder output and committed serialized artifact conformance are treated as separate claims.
Scenes and prefabs move with `.meta` files; duplicate authoritative scenes are prohibited.
Runtime and visual evidence can override a static evaluator pass and return structured feedback to bounded repair.
Missing design is escalated rather than silently invented.
Parallelism, automatic merge, and autonomous dispatch remain disabled until a one-ticket lane is trustworthy.
structural_flaws: There is no end-to-end state machine connecting approved plan → writable execution → Git-observed changes → Unity validation → repair → human review → merge → delivery evidence → dependency readiness.

Moving canon is modeled as whole-document invalidation, not requirement-level versioning and impact. This will generate broad revalidation work while still failing to revise contracts whose meaning changed.

Unity asset authority is duplicated and already contradictory after one routine human-approved relocation. Structural validation passes because it verifies key consistency rather than target existence and GUID identity.
The current graph can label an item `single_agent` without resolving gameplay choices or proving its Unity integration surface is bounded; NSC-003 is the concrete counterexample.

A conformance record can be current while descriptive repository evidence inside its bound contract is factually stale, because only hashes, declared gates, and manually selected surfaces are evaluated.

The production runtime deliberately cannot write or execute approved commands, and the Unity runner remains an external manual operation. Therefore the current architecture is an audit/review platform, not an autonomous development pipeline.
The milestone ordering puts compact context, decomposition, provider parity, and generalized crew infrastructure ahead of the shortest working gameplay loop, despite the stated real-slice rule.

Worktree isolation alone does not solve Unity production integration. Each candidate still needs a viable Unity project/library strategy, serialized asset inspection, exclusive host execution, and post-rebase validation.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is not yet demonstrated. The architecture has materially improved safety, repeatability, and auditability, especially around Unity tests and camera validation. But at the frozen commit, zero tasks are dispatchable, providers cannot edit, NSC-003 is not safely specified, Unity validation is external, and evidence publication is manual. Recent history is overwhelmingly pipeline work with no new gameplay feature. The system is therefore slower than direct expert-assisted development today; it becomes plausibly high-leverage only after the proposed vertical slice proves a repeatable one-ticket cycle.
structured_output.verdict_reason: The foundational production instincts are strong, so this is not a fundamentally wrong approach. It is partially unsound because moving-design synchronization, Unity asset authority, and the execution-to-evidence path are either incorrectly framed or absent. The existing stale-scene contradiction is direct evidence that the current stores do not stay coherent, and the lack of a writable Unity delivery lane means the architecture cannot yet achieve its stated days-instead-of-weeks goal.
